title: Pocket Ops: GPU pool telemetry & action cards for quick SLO triage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a set of compact, tappable telemetry cards (Pocket Ops) for the Redwood Console dedicated capacity view. Purpose: enable on-call engineers and platform operators to triage GPU pool health and execute common actions (temporary burst, drain-node, scale-suggest) from a single-line card without opening the full pool detail view. Cards must surface SLO risk, 1‑hr cost delta if burst enabled, active alerts, and a single primary CTA. This ticket covers visual design, interaction specs, and prototype for a 3-card strip and a vertical stack variant for narrow panes.
acceptance_criteria: Three card variants designed: Healthy / Degraded / Critical, each with iconography, micro-metrics, and primary CTA
Cards show: pool name, short SLO status (green/amber/red), 5m latency P95, current utilization %, recent error spike flag, cost delta for enabling a 5-minute burst
Primary CTA maps to one of: Start Burst, Recommend Scale, or Open Pool Detail; secondary menu contains: Drain Node, Pause Autoscale, Copy Pool ID
Prototype (Figma) demonstrates hover, press, and keyboard focus states + confirmation microflow for destructive actions
Design tokens and spacing defined for compact 32px-height micro rows and 56px card variants
Accessibility: color contrast passes AA, icons have visible labels, keyboard-only users can trigger CTAs and secondary menus
Handoff doc includes annotated spec and sample API payloads for cost delta + SLO status endpoints
design_notes: Rationale: Ops teams often need an immediate surface for triage without loading heavy dashboards. Compact cards reduce context switching and align with mobile-first incident flows.
We prioritize a single clear action per card to reduce accidental escalations during paging events.
Cost delta should be pre-computed by backend to avoid incurring extra queries in the Console; display as +/- $0.XX over next 5 minutes and a tooltip with assumptions
Show a micro sparkline (16px tall) for last 10 minutes of latency to give trend context without taking space
Use new 'pill' SLO token (rounded rectangle) instead of full badges to keep vertical rhythm consistent with other compact components
prototypes: Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/pocket-ops-gpu-cards (prototype 0.2 includes vertical stack and strip)
Interactive: InVision stub for keyboard interactions: https://redwood-inv.io/pocket-ops-kbd-0-2
